definition_zh: 判断力；看法；判决；天谴
definition_en: the ability to form sound opinions, an opinion so formed, or a formal ruling by a court
core_image: 天平上的砝码落下，指针抖了一下，停住
scene: 评审室里，三位评委听完演奏，各自在纸上写下分数。Her judgment of the young pianist was kinder than the others'.
sceneCN: 这里 judgment 指「经思考形成的评价」（第 1 个义项：形成稳妥看法的能力及其结果）；句意为她对那位年轻钢琴家的评价比其他人宽厚。场景要素：评分纸、铅笔、舞台监听音箱。

pos.zh: 判断力；看法；判决；天谴

derivatives.zh: 与 judgment 同出拉丁语中「法官」一词，指审理者或审理这一行为
由拉丁语「法庭的」一词进入英语，指与司法有关的
由 judge 加形容词后缀构成，指有见地的、审慎的
由 judgmental 加副词后缀构成，指以评判的姿态；属另一条形容词线
由表「在前」的前缀加「判断」的拉丁词构成，指预先形成的判断，后指偏见

senses.title: The ability to form sound opinions
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh evidence and reach a sensible conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 权衡证据并得出合宜结论的能力
senses.example: Years of editing gave her a reliable judgment about which submissions would sell.
senses.exampleCN: 多年编辑经验让她对哪些投稿卖得动有可靠的判断。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it joins law and speaking, so judging originally meant declaring what is right, and the mental capacity sense grew from that authority.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁词把法律与言说连在一起，因此「判断」原指宣示何为正当，心智能力义由此权威感生长出来。

senses.title: An opinion reached
senses.definition: a conclusion one has come to about a person, work or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对人、作品或情形得出的结论
senses.example: My judgment is that the proposal is sound but the timing is wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 我的看法是方案本身可靠，但时机不对。
senses.why: Once the capacity produces something, the same noun names the product, which is why it appears with possessives.
senses.whyCN: 能力一旦产出结果，同一个名词就指那个结果，因此它常带所有格。

senses.title: A ruling by a court
senses.definition: the formal decision of a court that settles the rights of the parties
senses.definitionCN: 法院了结各方权利义务的正式决定
senses.example: The judgment ordered the company to restore the wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 判决责令该公司恢复这片湿地。
senses.why: Law was the earliest home of the word, and the courtroom sense never faded even as the everyday sense broadened.
senses.whyCN: 法律是这个词最早的家，即便日常义后来拓宽，法庭义也从未消退。

senses.title: A formal decision of a tribunal
senses.definition: an award or finding issued by a panel, arbitrator or competition jury
senses.definitionCN: 由评审团、仲裁人或竞赛评委作出的裁定或评定
senses.example: The arbitration judgment awarded costs to the smaller firm.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁裁决把费用判给了那家较小的公司。
senses.why: Any body that must settle a dispute borrows the courtroom noun, so the sense travels from courts to arbitrators and juries.
senses.whyCN: 任何必须了结争议的机构都会借用这个法庭名词，于是这一义从法院延伸到仲裁人与评委。

senses.title: The exercise of judicial authority
senses.definition: the act of deciding as one lawfully entitled to decide, as in the phrase to sit in judgment
senses.definitionCN: 以合法资格作出裁断的行为，如「坐在审判席上」这一说法
senses.example: The commission sits in judgment on complaints about broadcasters.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会对针对广播机构的投诉行使裁断权。
senses.why: The noun can name not just the ruling but the authority being exercised, which is why it survives in formal legal phrasing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指裁决，也指被行使的权威，因此它在正式法律措辞中留存。

senses.title: Divine judgment
senses.definition: in religious language, the verdict of a higher power on human conduct
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语言中，更高力量对人类行为的裁决
senses.example: The sermon warned of judgment and of mercy in the same breath.
senses.exampleCN: 布道在同一口气里既警告审判，也提到怜悯。
senses.why: Religious language took the courtroom image and moved the judge upward, so the word acquired a sense no human court can supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言借走法庭意象，把审判者移到天上，这个词于是获得人间法庭给不了的义项。

senses.title: Critical evaluation in a field
senses.definition: the trained assessment of quality in a craft, as in editorial or artistic judgment
senses.definitionCN: 对某一行业或艺术品质的专业评估
senses.example: The curator's judgment on the drawings was trusted by three museums.
senses.exampleCN: 这位策展人对这批素描的品评得到三家博物馆信赖。
senses.why: Where a field has standards but no rules, practitioners rely on trained judgment, and the word names that reliance.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域有标准却无规则时，从业者依赖训练出的判断，这个词就指这种依赖。

senses.title: A judgment call
senses.definition: a decision that must rest on opinion because the rules and data leave the case open
senses.definitionCN: 规则与数据都未定论、只能凭看法作出的决定
senses.example: Whether to publish before the holiday was a judgment call.
senses.exampleCN: 要不要在假期前发表，是个只能凭判断的决定。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks the point where calculation stops and opinion must act, which is the everyday survival of the old authority sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法标出计算终止、看法必须上场的那一刻，也是古老权威义在日常中的遗留。

intro.en: Judgment comes through Old French from Latin judicium, built on judex 'judge', which joins jus 'law, right' to dicere 'to say, declare'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judgment 经古法语来自拉丁语 judicium，其基础是 judex「法官」，由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Jus meant 'law, right, justice'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to the verb for swearing an oath is a hypothesis.
items.cn: jus 意为「法律、权利、正义」。其更早来源未得到证明；有人提出它与表「发誓」的动词有关，那只是假说。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. The same verb builds dictate, predict and verdict.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、宣告」。同一个动词还构成 dictate、predict 与 verdict。

items.en: Jus plus dicere produced judex 'one who declares the law', hence the judge.
items.cn: jus 加 dicere 构成 judex「宣告法律的人」，即法官。

items.en: The noun judicium named the declaring of a right, then the ruling itself and the faculty of ruling well.
items.cn: 名词 judicium 既指宣告权利，也指裁决本身，以及善于裁断的能力。

items.en: Old French jugement carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where legal use came first and general use followed.
items.cn: 古法语 jugement 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，法律用法先行，一般用法随后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of jus is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；jus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are routinely mixed up with judgment; group two holds near neighbours for an opinion or a ruling.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，常与本词张冠李戴；第二组是表示看法或裁定的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the official and the verb for what that official does; judgment is the ruling or the capacity, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 作名词指法官，作动词指法官所做的事；judgment 指裁决或能力，不指人。

entries.definition: An adjective for the court system and its procedures, not for a person's opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容法院系统及其程序，而非个人的看法。

entries.definition: Built to mean full of good judgment, so it is a compliment; it is not the adjective of judgmental.
entries.definitionCN: 构成上意为「富于良好判断」，因此是褒义；它并不是 judgmental 的形容词原形。

entries.definition: Built with the prefix meaning 'before' plus the same judging root, so it literally means a judgment formed in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「在前」的前缀加同一个「判断」词根构成，字面就是「事先形成的判断」。

entries.definition: The formal finding of a jury, literally a true saying; it is the courtroom sense of judgment made specific.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪审团的正式认定，字面是「如实说出」，是法院义的具体化。

entries.definition: A view held without the weight of authority; judgment suggests that the view was earned by weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 指所持的看法，不带权威分量；judgment 暗示这看法是权衡得来的。

entries.definition: The process or result of measuring something against criteria; judgment adds the personal act of deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 指按标准衡量的过程或结果；judgment 多了「人作出裁断」这一层。

entries.definition: The ability to see subtle differences, especially in quality; judgment stresses the conclusion rather than the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 指看出细微差别的能力，尤其在品质上；judgment 强调结论而非看见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、真实的词族与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: The Latin noun joins law and declaring, so judgment is law spoken out loud.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁名词把「法律」与「宣告」连在一起，因此判断就是被说出来的法。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, judicious, judiciary, prejudice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、judicious、judiciary、prejudice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the courtroom origin: pass judgment, sit in judgment, a court judgment.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出法庭出身：作出评判、坐在审判席上、法院判决。

normal.en: The everyday phrase a judgment call marks the point where rules run out.
normal.cn: 日常说法「凭判断的决定」标出规则用尽的那一刻。

normal.en: British writing often spells the noun judgement, while American writing prefers judgment.
normal.cn: 英式写作常拼作 judgement，美式写作多用 judgment。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose pointer stops only after the weights are all placed.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，砝码全部放好之后指针才停住。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel that falls once and ends every argument in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一把法槌落下一次，房间里所有争论就此结束。

abstract.en: Picture a critic who looks at a painting for a long time before saying a single word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位评论家看画很久，才说出一句话。

examples.en: The recruiter trusted her judgment more than the test scores.
examples.cn: 招聘者更信她的判断，而不是那些测验分数。

examples.en: The court issued a judgment that reopened the old case.
examples.cn: 法院作出判决，让这桩旧案重新开庭。

examples.en: Whether to speak now or wait was a judgment call.
examples.cn: 现在开口还是再等等，是个只能凭判断的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「judge 法官 + ment 行为」——法官作出的，就是判决与判断

root: 拉丁 judicium「裁断」= judex「法官」+ 名词后缀；judex 又由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成；jus 更深来源不确定。英语 judgment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of declaring what is right: a capacity, an opinion, a court's ruling, an arbitrator's award, the authority behind it, a heavenly verdict, a craft's evaluation and a call made where rules stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：宣告何为正当。它依次是能力、看法、法院判决、仲裁裁定、背后的权威、天上的裁决、行业内的品评，以及规则用尽处凭看法作出的决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose pointer trembles and then stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上的指针抖了一下，然后停住。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND PRODUCT: the ability to weigh and the opinion it produces are the same act seen inside and outside.
branches.cn: 能力与产物：权衡的能力与它产出的看法，是同一动作的内外两面。

branches.en: COURT AND AUTHORITY: a ruling and the lawful power to issue it are inseparable in legal use.
branches.cn: 判决与权威：在法律用法里，裁决与作出裁决的合法权力不可分。

branches.en: BORROWED COURTROOM: arbitrators and juries use the noun because they too must end a dispute.
branches.cn: 借来的法庭：仲裁人与评委也用这个名词，因为他们同样必须了结争议。

branches.en: UPWARD VERDICT: religion moves the judge above the room, adding a sense no human court supplies.
branches.cn: 向上的裁决：宗教把审判者移到房间之上，增添了人间法庭给不了的义项。

branches.en: TRAINED AND OPEN CASES: professional evaluation and the judgment call both act where written rules fall silent.
branches.cn: 专业与开放情形：行业品评与凭判断的决定，都在明文规则沉默处发挥作用。

intro.en: Judgment is two Latin pieces plus a Latin noun suffix, and the pieces also build the rest of the legal family.
intro.cn: judgment 由两个拉丁成分加一个拉丁名词后缀构成，这些成分还构成整个法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus gives justice, jurist and jury; Latin dicere gives dictate, predict, verdict and the same ending in prejudice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 jus 衍生 justice、jurist 与 jury；拉丁 dicere 衍生 dictate、predict、verdict，以及 prejudice 中的同一成分。

items.example: The root supplies the legal half of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词义中「法」的那一半。

items.example: The root supplies the speaking that makes a ruling official.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供使裁决成为正式的那种言说。

items.example: The compound produced the name of the official.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词造出了官员的名称。

items.example: The noun is the base that French and English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是法语与英语借用的基础。

items.example: The suffix marks the ruling as something produced and recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把裁决标为被产出、被记录之物。

items.meaning: a ruling or a formed opinion
items.example: English keeps one noun for the act, the result and the capacity.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个名词指行为、结果与能力。

items.example: The person noun survives beside the abstract one.
items.exampleCN: 指人的名词与抽象名词并存。

items.example: The adjective stays inside the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词留在法律义之内。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun of office into an adjective of system.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把职务名词变成制度形容词。

definition_zh: 果汁；汁液；精髓
definition_en: the liquid squeezed from fruit, vegetables, or meat, or the essential energy of something
core_image: 一只手把橙子对半切开，用力一挤，汁顺着指缝流下来
scene: 夏天的厨房里，桌上摊着果皮和切板，杯子里是刚榨出来的橙红色。A glass of fresh juice is all she wants at breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 juice 是「果汁」（第 1 个义项：从果实压出的液体），句意为早餐她只想要一杯鲜果汁。画面里的物件：橙子、切板、玻璃杯。

pos.zh: 名词：果汁；汁液；精髓

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「多汁的；有看头的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「榨汁机」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「无汁的」

senses.title: Liquid from fruit
senses.definition: the liquid pressed or squeezed out of fruit or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 从果实或蔬菜中压出的液体
senses.example: She drinks a glass of carrot juice every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上喝一杯胡萝卜汁。
senses.why: The fruit sense is the one English uses every day.
senses.whyCN: 果实的义项是英语每天在用的那一个。

senses.title: Liquid from meat
senses.definition: the natural liquid released from cooked meat
senses.definitionCN: 熟肉里自然渗出的液体
senses.example: Let the chicken rest so the juices stay in.
senses.exampleCN: 让鸡肉静置一会儿，肉汁才不会流失。
senses.why: Meat keeps the older, kitchen sense of the Latin word.
senses.whyCN: 肉汁保留了拉丁词更古老的厨房义。

senses.title: Energy or essence
senses.definition: the power that runs something, or the most essential part of it
senses.definitionCN: 让某物运转的动力，或某物最精华的部分
senses.example: The old radio needs new batteries; it has run out of juice.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老收音机要换电池，它没电了。
senses.why: Modern speech borrowed the liquid image for electric power, then for any energy.
senses.whyCN: 现代口语借「汁」的意象指电力，再扩展到任何能量。

intro.en: Juice came through Old French from Latin jus, which meant broth or juice.
intro.cn: juice 经古法语来自拉丁语 jus，意为肉汤或汁液。

items.en: jus meant "broth, juice, sauce".
items.cn: jus 意为「肉汤、汁、调味汁」。

items.en: French took it as jus, still used for gravy and law.
items.cn: 法语作 jus，既指肉汁也指法。

items.en: The form jus was borrowed into English as juice.
items.cn: jus 这一形式被英语借作 juice。

items.en: English used juice for the liquid of plants and fruit.
items.cn: 英语用 juice 指植物与果实的汁液。

items.en: Electricity gave the word a modern second life.
items.cn: 电力让这个词获得了现代的第二生命。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jui- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for liquid and its essence.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jui- 开头；近义组收表示液体及其精华的词。

entries.definition: Full of juice, or full of interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「多汁的；有看头的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A machine for pressing fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「榨汁机」，同族词。

entries.definition: Very large of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「特大号的」，拼写开头相同。

entries.definition: The liquid that carries food through a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「树液」，植物生理用词。

entries.definition: Anything that flows and takes the shape of its vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「液体」，最泛。

entries.definition: The most important quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「精华」，偏抽象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks jump from a squeezed orange to a dying battery.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个挤开的橙子跳到快没电的电池。

normal.en: jus in Latin was broth or juice.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jus 是肉汤或汁。

normal.en: Squeeze an orange and the juice is what leaves.
normal.cn: 挤一个橙子，离开的就是汁。

normal.en: Add -y and the fruit becomes juicy.
normal.cn: 加 -y，果实就有了汁。

normal.en: A juicer is the machine that does the squeezing.
normal.cn: juicer 就是干这挤活的机器。

normal.en: A device without power has run out of juice too.
normal.cn: 没电的装置，也被说成「没汁了」。

abstract.en: Juice is the inside of a fruit made visible.
abstract.cn: 汁是果实内部露出来的样子。

abstract.en: What is squeezed out loses its shape but keeps its taste.
abstract.cn: 被挤出来的东西失了形状，却保住了味道。

abstract.en: Every engine lives on some kind of juice.
abstract.cn: 每台机器都靠某种「汁」活着。

examples.en: The children shared a carton of apple juice.
examples.cn: 孩子们分喝了一盒苹果汁。

examples.en: Lemon juice keeps sliced apples from browning.
examples.cn: 柠檬汁能让切开的苹果不变褐。

examples.en: The team has plenty of juice left for the last round.
examples.cn: 这支队伍还有足够的体力打最后一轮。

dict_mnemonic.text: juice 与 jus 同形：挤出来的东西

root: 拉丁语 jus「肉汤；汁」→ 古法语 jus → 中古英语 juice。同源有 justice（法）；派生有 juicy、juicer、juiceless。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: fruit liquid, meat juices, and the energy or essence that keeps something going.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：果实汁液、肉汁，以及维持某物的能量或精华。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orange halved and pressed until liquid runs down the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：橙子被挤开，汁顺着手指往下流。

branches.en: THE GLASS: fruit pressed into a drink.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：果实被压成饮料。

branches.en: THE PLATE: meat keeping its liquid on the board.
branches.cn: 盘子这条线：肉在案板上留住汁水。

branches.en: THE BATTERY: the power that makes a thing run.
branches.cn: 电池这条线：让东西运转的动力。

branches.en: THE SQUEEZE: both senses are liquid taken from something.
branches.cn: 挤压这条线：两个义项都是从某物里取出的液体。

branches.en: THE CORE: what is inside is also what is essential.
branches.cn: 内核这条线：里面的东西也就是精华。

intro.en: Juice is a whole Latin stem borrowed through French, with a silent-e ending in English.
intro.cn: juice 是经法语借来的完整拉丁词干，英语里带一个不发音的 -e。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus stands behind juice; justice comes from the same Latin stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jus 是 juice 的前身，justice 也出自同一词干。

items.example: It marks the long vowel in juice.
items.exampleCN: 它标出 juice 的长元音。

definition_zh: 跳；跳跃；猛涨；跳过
definition_en: to push yourself off a surface into the air, or to rise or increase suddenly
core_image: 两脚同时离开地面，身体在半空中停住一瞬
scene: 跑道尽头，一个孩子数着数，腿一弯就蹬了出去。He jumped the fence and ran across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 jump 是「跳」（第 1 个义项：双脚蹬离地面），句意为他翻过栅栏穿过田野跑开。画面里的物件：跑道、栅栏、草地。

pos.zh: 动词：跳；跳跃；猛涨；跳过
名词：跳跃；猛增

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者；毛衣（英式）」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃运动」

senses.title: Pushing off the ground
senses.definition: to leave the ground by bending the legs and pushing hard
senses.definitionCN: 屈腿用力蹬地离开地面
senses.example: The dog jumped into the water without hesitating.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗毫不犹豫地跳进水里。
senses.why: The physical sense is the core, and every other use borrows its upward push.
senses.whyCN: 身体动作是核心，其他用法都借了那股向上的蹬力。

senses.title: Rising suddenly
senses.definition: to increase or rise quickly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 迅速大幅度上升
senses.example: Prices jumped by a third in one month.
senses.exampleCN: 价格一个月里猛涨了三分之一。
senses.why: Numbers that rise suddenly behave like something springing up.
senses.whyCN: 突然上升的数字，像有东西弹了起来。

senses.title: Skipping over something
senses.definition: to cross over a fence or gap in one movement
senses.definitionCN: 一个动作跨过栅栏或空隙
senses.example: She jumped the low wall and was gone.
senses.exampleCN: 她跳过矮墙就不见了。
senses.why: The jump also covers the object jumped over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也涵盖被跳过去的那个东西。

senses.title: Moving on too fast
senses.definition: to pass to a later point without the proper steps
senses.definitionCN: 跳过应有的步骤直接进入后面
senses.example: Do not jump to conclusions before the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 检查结果出来之前别急着下结论。
senses.why: Thinking can leap too, and skipping steps is the risky version.
senses.whyCN: 思维也会跳，跳过步骤就是有风险的那种。

intro.en: Jump is probably imitative, an English word of uncertain origin that simply sounds like a spring.
intro.cn: jump 很可能是拟声词，来源不确定，读音本身就带着一弹。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century with no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: 这个词十六世纪出现在英语中，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: It was used of leaping animals and people alike.
items.cn: 它同时用于跳跃的动物和人。

items.en: The sense of a sudden rise in price came early.
items.cn: 价格猛涨的义项很早就出现了。

items.en: Sport fixed compounds such as long jump and high jump.
items.cn: 体育固定了 long jump、high jump 这样的复合词。

items.en: Idioms like jump at a chance keep the suddenness.
items.cn: jump at a chance 一类成语保留着那种突然。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the j- and -ump shape; the near-meaning group holds words for leaving the ground.
note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 与 -ump 的外形；近义组收表示离开地面的词。

entries.definition: One who jumps, or a knitted top.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「跳跃者；毛衣」，同族词。

entries.definition: Easily startled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「容易受惊的」，同族词。

entries.definition: To knock against something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「碰撞」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To spring a long way through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「跃」，距离更远。

entries.definition: To move on one leg or in small jumps.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「单脚跳」，幅度小。

entries.definition: To move suddenly upward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「弹起」，强调弹力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks stay with the short, springy sound of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子跟着这个词短促而有弹性的音。

normal.en: Say it fast and the mouth itself springs.
normal.cn: 快说一遍，嘴巴自己就弹了一下。

normal.en: No Latin behind it: the sound is the origin.
normal.cn: 背后没有拉丁语，声音就是来源。

normal.en: Prices jump like a startled animal.
normal.cn: 价格惊跳起来，像受惊的动物。

normal.en: Jump at a chance: the leap comes first, the thought later.
normal.cn: jump at a chance：先跳，后想。

normal.en: Add -y and you are jumpy, ready to startle.
normal.cn: 加 -y 就是 jumpy，随时会惊跳。

abstract.en: A jump is a small rebellion against gravity.
abstract.cn: 跳跃是对重力的一次小小反叛。

abstract.en: What goes up owes the ground a return.
abstract.cn: 跳起来的东西，都欠地面一次回程。

abstract.en: Most leaps are decided before the feet leave.
abstract.cn: 多数跃起，在脚离地之前就决定了。

examples.en: She jumped off the wall and landed badly.
examples.cn: 她从墙上跳下来，落地时扭到了。

examples.en: Sales jumped in the week before the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期前那一周销量猛增。

examples.en: Try not to jump from one idea to the next.
examples.cn: 尽量别从一个念头跳到下一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: jump 读音短促，本身就带一个弹起来的感觉

root: 来源不确定，可能为拟声词，十六世纪出现于英语。派生有 jumper、jumpy；无拉丁语同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: leaving the ground, rising fast, crossing in one move, and skipping ahead.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：蹬地跃起、迅速上升、一跨而过，以及跳过步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: both feet leaving the ground and hanging for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚离地，在半空停住一瞬。

branches.en: THE AIR: the body in flight.
branches.cn: 空中这条线：腾起的身体。

branches.en: THE CHART: a line that leaps upward.
branches.cn: 曲线这条线：一下窜上去的线。

branches.en: THE WALL: the fence taken in one move.
branches.cn: 矮墙这条线：一步跨过去的栅栏。

branches.en: THE GAP: steps left out on purpose or by haste.
branches.cn: 空缺这条线：有意或匆忙落下的步骤。

branches.en: THE SURPRISE: both senses break an expected line.
branches.cn: 意外这条线：两个义项都打断了预期。

intro.en: Jump has no prefix or suffix in its base form; it is a single Germanic-style root of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: jump 原形没有前后缀，是一个来源不明的单一词根。

latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，所以 latinEntries 留空。

definition_zh: 套头毛衣；针织罩衫；跳跃者；跳高运动员；跨接线索
definition_en: a knitted garment pulled on over the head; also a person or animal that jumps, or a small wire used to connect points in a circuit
core_image: 一件从头上往下套的厚针织衫，或者一个正腾空跃起的人
scene: 山上的清晨很冷，她把自己裹得严严实实才出门。She pulled on a warm wool jumper before stepping into the frosty morning.
sceneCN: 这里 jumper 是「套头毛衣、针织罩衫」（第 1 个义项：从头上套穿的针织衣物）；句意是她在清晨霜冷出门前套上一件厚羊毛衫。

pos.zh: 套头毛衣；针织罩衫（英式）
跳跃者；跳高运动员
跨接线索；（美式）无袖连衣裙式外衣

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「跳；跃起」，jumper 加名词后缀 -er 表人
动词 jump 的动名词形式，义为「跳跃运动」
由 jump 加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的；神经质的」

senses.title: A knitted garment pulled on over the head
senses.definition: a knitted piece of clothing, usually woollen, that you pull on over your head to keep warm
senses.definitionCN: 一种针织衣物，多为毛线织成，从头上往下套穿以保暖，即英式英语里的毛衣
senses.example: He wore a grey jumper over his shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 他在衬衫外面套了一件灰色毛衣。
senses.why: The noun is jump plus the agent suffix -er, and the garment is named after the action of jumping into it: you pull it over your head in one quick motion.
senses.whyCN: 名词由 jump 加表物/人的后缀 -er 构成；这种衣物因「一下套进去」像跳进去的动作而得名，故称 jumper。

senses.title: A person or animal that jumps
senses.titleCN: 跳跃者；跳高（跳远）运动员
senses.definition: a person or animal that jumps, especially an athlete who competes in jumping events
senses.definitionCN: 会跳跃的人或动物，尤指参加跳高、跳远等跳跃项目的运动员
senses.example: She is the best long jumper on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是队里最出色的跳远选手。
senses.why: This is the direct agent reading: jump plus -er names the doer of the action, following the same pattern as runner and swimmer.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直接的动作执行者含义：jump 加 -er 表「做跳跃动作的人」，与 runner（跑步者）、swimmer（游泳者）构词方式一致。

senses.title: A short wire connecting two points in a circuit
senses.definition: a small piece of wire with a connector at each end, used to link two points in an electronic circuit
senses.definitionCN: 两端带接头的短导线，用于在电路中把两个点临时连接起来，也叫跨接线
senses.example: Connect the two terminals with a jumper.
senses.exampleCN: 用一根跨接线把两个接线端连起来。
senses.why: The wire figuratively jumps across a gap in the circuit, so the jumping image is transferred to an object that bridges a space.
senses.whyCN: 这根线像是在电路的空隙间「跳过去」，跳跃意象被转移到跨越间隙的实物上。

senses.title: A sleeveless dress worn over a blouse (American)
senses.definition: in American English, a sleeveless dress worn over a blouse or sweater
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指罩在衬衫或毛衣外面的无袖连衣裙式外衣
senses.example: The school uniform includes a navy jumper.
senses.exampleCN: 校服包括一件藏青色无袖背心裙。
senses.why: In American usage the word drifted from the knitted top to the pinafore-style dress worn on top of other clothes, keeping the idea of a garment put on over another layer.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法从针织上衣漂移到罩在外面的背心式连衣裙，保留了「套穿在其他衣物外层」的核心意象。

senses.title: A loose outer garment or blanket-like cape (older use)
senses.definition: in older English, a loose outer garment or a blanket-like cape worn by women or workers
senses.definitionCN: 旧式英语中指宽松的罩衣或毯子似的披巾，多为妇女或劳动者所穿
senses.example: She wrapped a heavy jumper around her shoulders against the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一件厚实的罩衣裹在肩上御寒。
senses.why: This is the historical layer: the word first named a loose overgarment, and the modern sweater sense grew out of this earlier clothing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是历史层次：该词最初指宽松罩衣，现代「毛衣」义正是从这层衣物含义演化而来。

intro.en: Jumper comes from the verb jump plus the suffix -er. The clothing sense is generally traced to a loose overgarment first recorded in the seventeenth century, though the exact reason the garment was named after jumping is uncertain.
intro.cn: jumper 由动词 jump 加后缀 -er 构成。衣物义一般认为始于十七世纪记录的一种宽松罩衣，但这种衣物为何以「跳」命名，确切原因已不可考。

items.en: The verb jump first appears in English in the early seventeenth century; its deeper origin is uncertain, with proposed links to Germanic imitative roots expressing bouncing or thudding movement. Any earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 动词 jump 最早于十七世纪初见于英语；其更深的来源不确定，有观点认为与日耳曼语族模仿弹跳、砰然动作的拟声词根有关。更早的形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Jump emerges as a common verb for leaping, quickly replacing older native verbs such as leap in many everyday contexts.
items.cn: jump 作为表示跳跃的常用动词出现，在日常语境中迅速取代 leap 等更古老的本土动词。

items.en: Jumper is first recorded meaning a loose outer garment or cape. Why this garment was called a jumper is uncertain; a common suggestion is the idea of leaping or slipping into it quickly, but this remains conjecture.
items.cn: jumper 首次被记录为「宽松罩衣、披巾」义。这种衣物为何叫 jumper 已不可考；常见的一种解释是「迅速跳进去穿上」的联想，但这只是推测。

items.en: The agent sense, a person who jumps, develops naturally from jump plus -er, and gains a sporting flavour as athletics competitions formalise events such as the long jump and high jump.
items.cn: 表人的「跳跃者」义由 jump 加 -er 自然发展而来；随着跳远、跳高等田径项目正规化，这一含义带上体育色彩。

items.en: In British English, jumper narrows to mean a knitted sweater pulled on over the head, and becomes one of the most common everyday words for this garment.
items.cn: 在英式英语中，jumper 词义收窄为「从头上套穿的针织毛衣」，成为这类衣物最常用的日常叫法之一。

items.en: In American English the clothing sense instead refers to a sleeveless pinafore dress worn over a blouse, and a separate technical sense, a connecting wire in a circuit, appears in electrical usage.
items.cn: 美式英语中衣物义转指罩在衬衫外的无袖背心裙；电学用法中另出现「跨接线」这一技术含义。

note.en: Jumper looks and sounds close to several other words, and its meanings differ sharply between British and American English, so context matters.
note.cn: jumper 与若干词形相近的词容易混淆，且英式、美式含义差别很大，需结合语境判断。

entries.definition: to push yourself off the ground and into the air using your legs
entries.definitionCN: 蹬地跃起；跳；基础动词，是 jumper 的构词来源

entries.definition: nervous and easily frightened, as if always about to jump
entries.definitionCN: 紧张不安的；一惊一乍的；由 jump 加 -y 构成的形容词

entries.definition: a pair of wires used to connect one car battery to another
entries.definitionCN: 搭火线；跨接电缆，用于连接两辆车的电瓶，属复合名词

entries.definition: a knitted garment for the upper body; the common American equivalent of the British jumper
entries.definitionCN: 毛衣；美式英语中的常用对应词，与英式 jumper 第一义相同

entries.definition: a knitted top without buttons that you pull over your head
entries.definitionCN: 套头衫；与套穿毛衣义相近，强调无扣、从头上套穿

entries.definition: a sleeveless garment worn over a blouse, close to the American jumper dress
entries.definitionCN: 围裙式罩衣；背心裙，与美式 jumper 第四义相近

normalIntro.en: Use the base word jump and real word patterns to fix the meanings in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住基础词 jump 与真实构词、搭配规律，把各个含义钉进记忆。

normal.en: jump + -er = jumper: the doer of jumping, a person who jumps.
normal.cn: jump 加 -er 表人：跳跃者、跳高跳远运动员，这是最直白的构词。

normal.en: The sweater sense comes from the image of jumping into the garment: pull it over your head in one quick move.
normal.cn: 毛衣义来自「一下跳进去穿上」的画面：把衣服从头上快速套下。

normal.en: In Britain say jumper for a wool sweater; in America jumper is a pinafore dress — same word, different clothes.
normal.cn: 英国人说 jumper 指毛线衫；美国人说的 jumper 是无袖背心裙——同一个词指不同的衣服。

normal.en: In electronics a jumper jumps across a gap, connecting two points with a short wire.
normal.cn: 电子学里 jumper 是「跳过」空隙的短线，把电路中两个点连起来。

normal.en: Collocations to lock in: pull on a jumper, a chunky jumper, jumper cable.
normal.cn: 记牢这些搭配：pull on a jumper（套上毛衣）、a chunky jumper（厚毛衣）、jumper cable（搭火线）。

abstract.en: One motion, into the air: jump is a single explosive movement — the jumper rides that movement, whether person, garment, or wire.
abstract.cn: 一个腾空的动作：jump 是爆发性的一跳——无论人、衣服还是电线，jumper 都乘着这一跳。

abstract.en: Picture winter mornings: the thick wool jumper waiting by the bed, the first warm thing you jump into.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日清晨：厚毛线衫立在床边，是一天里第一个想钻进去的温暖之物。

abstract.en: A bridge in miniature: the jumper wire leaps a tiny valley of empty circuit board to make the connection.
abstract.cn: 微型桥梁：跨接线在电路板的空隙间一跃而过，完成连接。

examples.en: She knitted a blue jumper for her grandson last winter.
examples.cn: 去年冬天她给孙子织了一件蓝色毛衣。

examples.en: The young jumper cleared a personal best of two metres in the high jump final.
examples.cn: 这位年轻的跳高运动员在决赛中跳出了两米的个人最好成绩。

examples.en: It was so cold that he pulled on a thick jumper before going out.
examples.cn: 天太冷了，他出门前套上了一件厚毛衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「跳馍儿」——像跳进一碗热腾腾的馍汤里一样，把毛衣从头上一下套进去，暖意扑面。

root: jumper 由动词 jump（跳）加名词后缀 -er 构成。jump 的更早词源不确定，一般认为可能与日耳曼语族表弹跳动作的拟声词根有关，属重构形式；-er 是英语本土的施动/器物后缀， jumper 的「毛衣」义经由「跳进去穿上」的动作联想得名（此解释存疑，仅为常见推测）。

sensesIntro.en: From the single image of a jump, the word spreads to the garment you jump into, the person who jumps, the wire that jumps a gap, and older dress meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「一跳」这一个画面出发，词义延伸到跳进去穿的衣服、跳跃的人、跨越空隙的导线，以及旧式的罩衣裙装含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one leap — into a garment, over a gap, or off the ground
core.cn: 核心意象：一次腾跳——跳进衣服、跃过空隙、或蹬地而起

branches.en: The literal agent: an athlete or animal that jumps.
branches.cn: 最字面的施动者：跳跃的运动员或动物。

branches.en: The clothing line: from loose overgarment to knitted sweater.
branches.cn: 衣物一线：从宽松罩衣到针织毛衣。

branches.en: The American dress layer: sleeveless garment over a blouse.
branches.cn: 美式裙装层：罩在衬衫外的无袖背心裙。

branches.en: The technical transfer: a wire that jumps across a gap in a circuit.
branches.cn: 技术性转义：跨越电路空隙的导线。

branches.en: Everyday anchors: the two most common senses a learner meets first.
branches.cn: 日常锚点：学习者最先接触的两个高频义项。

intro.en: Jumper is built with a native English agent suffix, and its family shows how -er turns actions into doers and things.
intro.cn: jumper 由英语本土表人后缀 -er 构成；其词族展示了 -er 如何把动作变成「做动作的人或物」。

latinIntro.en: The jump- family is Germanic rather than Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the suffixes below are English and French borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: jump 词族属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，因此没有拉丁同源词可列；下面的后缀均为英语本土或法语借入的构词成分。

core_image: 队列里排在后面、个子还矮一头的那个新人
scene: 办公室里最新的那个人坐在靠门的位置，桌上只摆着一台旧电脑。As a junior clerk, he handled the files nobody else wanted.
sceneCN: 这里 junior 是「初级的、资历浅的」（第 1 个义项：在职位或经验上低于他人），句意为作为初级职员，他处理没人愿意管的档案。画面里的物件：办公室、靠门的桌子、旧电脑。

pos.zh: 形容词：年少的；初级的；资历浅的；下级的
名词：较年轻者；下级；初级职员

derivatives.zh: 由 junior 加 -ity 构成，义为「资历较浅的状态」
由 junior 加 -ate 构成，指修会培养期或初级阶段

senses.title: Lower in rank or experience
senses.definition: having a lower position or less experience than others in the same organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构中职位较低或经验较少
senses.example: She started as a junior designer in the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工作室从初级设计师做起。
senses.why: Rank is the comparison that matters most in offices, staff against staff.
senses.whyCN: 在办公室里最重要的比较是职位，是员工与员工之间的比较。

senses.title: Younger in age
senses.definition: younger than another person, often used of a son named after his father
senses.definitionCN: 年龄小于他人，常用于父子同名的场合
senses.example: He is three years junior to his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他比哥哥小三岁。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply younger, and it still keeps the Latin comparison.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思就是「更年轻」，它仍保留着拉丁语比较级的底子。

senses.title: Of the lower school level
senses.definition: relating to the earlier part of a school or a college year
senses.definitionCN: 指学校的低年级阶段或大学三年级
senses.example: She teaches at a junior school near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公园附近的一所小学教书。
senses.why: Schools borrow the age comparison and turn it into a stage of study.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了年龄比较，把它变成一个学段。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who holds a lower position than someone else
senses.definitionCN: 职位低于他人的人
senses.example: The partners rarely listen to the juniors.
senses.exampleCN: 合伙人很少听下属的意见。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a person: the lower-ranked member of the team.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成一个人：团队中位次较低的那个成员。

senses.title: Smaller in a competition class
senses.definition: belonging to a younger age group in sport or contests
senses.definitionCN: 指体育或竞赛中属于较年轻年龄组
senses.example: He won the junior title at fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十五岁就拿下了少年组冠军。
senses.why: Sport turns age into a class, with its own titles and records.
senses.whyCN: 体育把年龄变成一个组别，有自己的冠军和纪录。

senses.title: The third college year
senses.definition: in American usage, the third year of a four-year course
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指四年制课程的第三年
senses.example: She spent her junior year abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她大三那年去了国外。
senses.why: In a four-year course the third year is junior to the last one.
senses.whyCN: 在四年制课程里，第三年比上年一级「低」，于是叫 junior year。

intro.en: Junior was borrowed from Latin junior, the comparative of juvenis, young; English uses it unchanged.
intro.cn: junior 直接借自拉丁语 junior，是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级；英语原样沿用。

items.en: juvenis meant young, and junior was its comparative form.
items.cn: juvenis 意为年轻的，junior 是它的比较级。

items.en: The -or ending marks the comparative, as in senior.
items.cn: -or 词尾标记比较级，senior 也是如此。

items.en: English borrowed junior in the sixteenth century as an adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 junior，兼作形容词和名词。

items.en: The rank sense spread through offices and armed forces.
items.cn: 「职位较低」这一义在机关和军队中扩散。

items.en: The school senses, junior school and junior year, settled in the modern period.
items.cn: 初级学校与大学三年级等教育义在近现代固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives that end in -or; the near-meaning group holds words for younger and lower rank.
note.cn: 形近组收以 -or 结尾的拉丁比较级；近义组收表示年幼与低级的词。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: junior 的反义对应词，义为「年长的；高级的」。

entries.definition: Young, or a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于 juvenis，义为「少年的」。

entries.definition: The state of being junior.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指资历较浅的状态。

entries.definition: Less old than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 最简单直白的「更年轻的」。

entries.definition: Lower in rank within a system.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指体制中下级。

entries.definition: Someone being trained for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在受训的岗位新人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin comparative ending to the desk by the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语比较级词尾走到靠门的那张桌子。

normal.en: Junior is the comparative of juvenis, young.
normal.cn: junior 是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级。

normal.en: The pair junior and senior is fixed in offices and schools.
normal.cn: junior 与 senior 这一对在机关和学校都固定。

normal.en: Junior to someone uses to, not than.
normal.cn: junior to someone 用 to，不用 than。

normal.en: Junior high school covers the early teenage years.
normal.cn: junior high school 指初中阶段。

normal.en: In American colleges junior year is the third year.
normal.cn: 美国大学的 junior year 是第三年。

abstract.en: A junior is one row back in the same line.
abstract.cn: 初级者是在同一条队伍里后退一排的人。

abstract.en: The word is a comparison, so it always needs another person.
abstract.cn: 这个词是比较，因此总需要另一个人才成立。

abstract.en: Everyone is junior to someone, and senior to someone else.
abstract.cn: 每个人对某些人初级，对另一些人高级。

examples.en: Two junior staff members handled the whole report.
examples.cn: 两名初级员工完成了整份报告。

examples.en: My sister is junior to me by two years.
examples.cn: 我妹妹比我小两岁。

examples.en: He is looking for a junior position in design.
examples.cn: 他在找一个设计方面的初级职位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「就是你儿」—— 家里年纪最小的那个，就是初级选手

root: 拉丁语 juvenis「年轻的」→ 比较级 junior → 英语 junior，原样借用；同族的反义比较级是 senior。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: lower rank, younger age, lower school level, a lower-ranked person, a younger contest class, and the third college year.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：职位较低、年纪较小、学校初段、下级人员、少年组，以及大学三年级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing a row behind and half a head lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在后退一排、矮半头的位置。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a new desk and the files nobody wants.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：新桌子与没人要的档案。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the son who shares the father's name.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：与父亲同名的儿子。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: early years and the third college year.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：低年级与大学三年级。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the younger age bracket of a contest.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：比赛的较年轻年龄组。

branches.en: THE LADDER: every rung is junior to the one above.
branches.cn: 梯子这条线：每一级都低于它上面那一级。

intro.en: Junior is a Latin comparative borrowed whole; English adds only a few endings.
intro.cn: junior 是整体借来的拉丁比较级，英语只添了少数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all grow from juvenis, young.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都从 juvenis「年轻」长出来。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 junior 与 senior。

items.example: More junior is the periphrastic form.
items.exampleCN: more junior 是分析式比较级。

definition_zh: 陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团
definition_en: a group of ordinary people chosen to listen to a case and decide it, or a group that decides a competition
core_image: 十二个人坐在木栏后面，低头听完双方发言再做结论
scene: 法庭里空气很闷，旁听席坐满了人，栏杆后那一组人一直在记笔记。The jury returned after four hours with a clear verdict.
sceneCN: 这里 jury 是「陪审团」（第 1 个义项：依法听审并裁决的一组普通公民），句意为陪审团四小时后回来，给出了明确的裁决。画面里的物件：法庭、木栏、笔记本。

pos.zh: 名词：陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 jur- 加 -or 构成，指陪审员
由 jur- 加 -ist 构成，指法学家
由 jur- 加 -idical 构成，义为「司法上的」
由 jur- 加 dictio 构成，义为「司法管辖权」

senses.title: A body deciding a court case
senses.definition: a group of citizens sworn to hear evidence and give a verdict in a court
senses.definitionCN: 依法宣誓听取证据并在法庭上作出裁决的一组公民
senses.example: The jury took two days to reach a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团用了两天得出结论。
senses.why: The core sense is a sworn body that speaks a verdict for the court.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向法庭宣告裁决的一个宣誓团体。

senses.title: A panel judging a competition
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to judge a contest and choose winners
senses.definitionCN: 被选出为一比评优劣、决定获奖者的一组人
senses.example: The jury gave the prize to an unknown filmmaker.
senses.exampleCN: 评委会把奖给了一位无名导演。
senses.why: A contest panel judges the way a court does: it weighs and decides.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的评委与法庭一样评判：称量然后决定。

senses.title: Members collectively, with plural agreement
senses.definition: the group treated as a plural body in grammar, so the jury can be said to disagree
senses.definitionCN: 语法上按复数处理，因此可说陪审团意见不一致
senses.example: The jury were still arguing at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 到九点陪审团还在争论。
senses.why: British grammar lets a collective noun take a plural verb when the members act apart.
senses.whyCN: 英式语法允许集合名词在成员各自行动时接复数动词。

senses.title: A temporary makeshift device
senses.definition: a temporary arrangement in nautical or technical use, as a makeshift mast
senses.definitionCN: 航海或技术语境中的临时凑合装置，如临时桅杆
senses.example: They rigged a jury rudder after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后他们装了一副临时舵。
senses.why: Sailors use the word for a thing thrown together to meet an emergency.
senses.whyCN: 水手用这个词指为应付紧急情况匆匆凑成的东西。

senses.title: A body of citizens summoned by law
senses.definition: the body of citizens summoned to serve, seen as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被依法召集服役的公民群体，作为制度看待
senses.example: Jury service is a duty of the citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 担任陪审员是公民的义务。
senses.why: The institution side names not a case but the standing role of citizens in law.
senses.whyCN: 制度这一面指的不是某个案子，而是公民在法律中的常设角色。

intro.en: Jury comes from Old French juree, an oath, from Latin jurare, to swear, and shares the root jus, law.
intro.cn: jury 来自古法语 juree「誓言」，源自拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」，与 jus「法」同根。

items.en: jurare meant to swear an oath, and jus meant law or right.
items.cn: jurare 意为宣誓，jus 意为法或权利。

items.en: juree named a sworn body of men or the oath they took.
items.cn: juree 指宣誓组成的一群人，或他们所立的誓言。

items.en: English borrowed jury in the fourteenth century as the sworn body in a court.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 jury，指法庭上的宣誓团体。

items.en: The competition sense developed much later, as prizes became contests.
items.cn: 比赛评委义很晚才出现，源于评奖变成竞赛。

items.en: The nautical jury sense is separate and probably from a different source.
items.cn: 航海上的 jury 义是另一回事，很可能来源不同。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jur- root of law; the near-meaning group holds related bodies and legal roles.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-；近义组收相关机构与法律角色。

entries.definition: A member of a jury.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指陪审员。

entries.definition: An expert in law.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指法学家。

entries.definition: The authority of a court over a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指司法管辖权。

entries.definition: The decision a jury gives.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪审团作出的裁决。

entries.definition: A small group chosen to advise or judge.
entries.definitionCN: 指被选出评审或咨询的小组。

entries.definition: A body appointed to judge a special matter.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指审理专门事项的裁判机构。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the group to swearing an oath and to the contest panel.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个团体连到宣誓，也连到比赛的评委会。

normal.en: Latin jurare, to swear, is the parent of jury.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」是 jury 的亲本。

normal.en: Juror adds -or to the Latin root jur-.
normal.cn: juror 在拉丁词根 jur- 后加 -or。

normal.en: Jury is a collective noun, so a jury can be singular or plural in agreement.
normal.cn: jury 是集合名词，主谓一致可单可复。

normal.en: Grand jury is the American term for a group that decides charges.
normal.cn: grand jury 是美国指决定是否起诉的团体。

normal.en: Jury also judges cakes and films at festivals.
normal.cn: jury 在电影节和比赛里也评判作品。

abstract.en: A jury is twelve ordinary chairs pulled together to decide.
abstract.cn: 陪审团是十二把普通椅子凑在一起做决定。

abstract.en: They swear first and speak after.
abstract.cn: 他们先宣誓，后开口。

abstract.en: A group is trusted where a single voice might lean.
abstract.cn: 一个人可能偏，于是一群人被信任。

examples.en: The jury cleared him of all charges.
examples.cn: 陪审团洗清了他的全部指控。

examples.en: She was called for jury service in March.
examples.cn: 她三月被通知担任陪审员。

examples.en: A jury of five chose the winning film.
examples.cn: 由五人组成的评委会选出了获奖影片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「主意」—— 十几个人一起拿主意，就是陪审团

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」、jurare「宣誓」→ 古法语 juree「誓言；宣誓的一群人」→ 英语 jury。同族 juror、jurist、jurisdiction。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a sworn court body, a contest panel, its plural agreement, a nautical makeshift, and the institution of summoned citizens.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：法庭陪审团、比赛评委会、复数一致的用法、航海临时装置，以及被召集公民的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of ordinary people who swear and then decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群普通人先宣誓，再作决定。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: evidence heard from both sides.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：听取双方的证据。

branches.en: THE FESTIVAL: films watched and ranked.
branches.cn: 影展这条线：看片并排序。

branches.en: THE LATE ROOM: a group that has not agreed yet.
branches.cn: 深夜评议室这条线：还没取得一致的团体。

branches.en: THE STORM: a rudder lashed together in a hurry.
branches.cn: 风暴这条线：匆匆捆出的临时舵。

branches.en: THE SUMMONS: a letter that makes service a duty.
branches.cn: 传票这条线：一封信把服役变成义务。

intro.en: Jury is borrowed from French and shares the Latin law root jur- with many other words.
intro.cn: jury 从法语借来，与其他许多词共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus and jurare, law and to swear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus 与 jurare，即「法」与「宣誓」。

items.example: The word keeps the oath sense.

definition_zh: 正好；仅仅；刚刚；只是；公正的；恰好的
definition_en: exactly at that point, only a moment ago, merely, or fair and right
core_image: 一根线刚好对齐刻度，不多一分也不少一分
scene: 两个人在门口互相看了一眼，谁都没说话。He was just leaving when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 just 是「刚要」（第 1 个义项：正好处在某个时点上），句意为他正要出门时电话响了。画面里的物件：门口、外套、响起的电话。

pos.zh: 副词：正好；刚刚；仅仅；只是；简直
形容词：公正的；正当的；恰当的

derivatives.zh: 由 just 加 -ice 构成，义为「正义；司法」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
由 just 加 -ify 构成，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不公正的」

senses.title: Exactly at a point in time or space
senses.definition: exactly at a particular moment, or exactly at a place or amount
senses.definitionCN: 恰好在某一时刻，或恰好是某处、某个量
senses.example: The train arrived just as we reached the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚到闸口，火车就到了。
senses.why: The oldest core is exactness: neither earlier nor later, neither more nor less.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的核心是「恰好」：不早不晚，不多不少。

senses.title: A very short time ago
senses.definition: a very short time ago, in the immediate past
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚过去的一小段时间
senses.example: She has just called from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她刚从车站打来电话。
senses.why: A point so close to now that it barely qualifies as past.
senses.whyCN: 一个离现在极近的时刻，勉强算作过去。

senses.title: Only or merely
senses.definition: no more than the stated amount or thing
senses.definitionCN: 不超过所说的数量或事物
senses.example: It was just a small mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个小错误。
senses.why: Exactness narrows to a single item, leaving everything else outside.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」收窄到只有一个，其他都被排除在外。

senses.title: Fair according to what is right
senses.definition: acting or given in accordance with what is right and deserved
senses.definitionCN: 依照正当标准行事或给予的
senses.example: A just settlement was reached within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周内达成了公正的解决方案。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from exact measure to fair measure: what is deserved to a hair.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从精确的度量走到公平的度量：应得的一丝不差。

senses.title: Barely enough or almost not
senses.definition: only barely, so that the result is almost the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 指仅仅勉强达到，结果几乎相反
senses.example: We just made it before the gate closed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚好在关门前进去了。
senses.why: The exactness of just is stretched to its limit: one second more and it fails.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」被拉到极限：再多一秒就不成了。

senses.title: Used to soften a request or statement
senses.definition: in a request, used to make the tone lighter or politer
senses.definitionCN: 请求中用来让语气更轻或更客气
senses.example: Could you just wait outside for a moment?
senses.exampleCN: 你能在外面稍等一会儿吗？
senses.why: Just here lowers the weight of a request, asking for the smallest possible amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 just 减轻了请求的分量，只要求最小的那一点。

intro.en: Just comes from Latin justus, "lawful, right", from jus, law; the same word therefore covers both exactness and fairness.
intro.cn: just 来自拉丁语 justus「合法的、正当的」，源词 jus「法」；因此它同时覆盖「恰好」与「公正」两面。

items.en: jus meant law or right, and justus meant conforming to it.
items.cn: jus 意为法或权利，justus 意为符合法的。

items.en: Old French juste kept the sense of right and exactly fitting.
items.cn: 古法语 juste 保留了「正当」与「恰好合适」两种意思。

items.en: English borrowed just as both adjective and adverb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把 just 兼作形容词和副词借入。

items.en: The exactness sense, just right or just now, grew from fitting perfectly.
items.cn: 「恰好」义从「完全契合」发展而来。

items.en: The merely sense developed from the idea of exactly this and no more.
items.cn: 「仅仅」义从「恰好只有这些，不多」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jus root; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of time, degree, and fairness.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁 jus 词根；近义组收时间、程度与公平类副词。

entries.definition: Fairness, or the legal system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: In a fair way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」。

entries.definition: To show that something is right.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: No more than; merely.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「仅仅」，与第 3 个义项最近。

entries.definition: With no difference at all.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「恰好」，与第 1 个义项最近。

entries.definition: Treating people equally and rightly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「公平的」，与第 4 个义项最近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin law to the moment before the phone rings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「法」走到电话响前的那个瞬间。

normal.en: Latin jus, law, is the root of just, justice, and justify.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jus「法」是 just、justice、justify 的共同词根。

normal.en: Just as means at the same instant that something else happens.
normal.cn: just as 表示另一件事正在发生的同一瞬间。

normal.en: Just now means a moment ago, not at this instant.
normal.cn: just now 指刚才，而不是此刻。

normal.en: Just a moment is the polite way to ask for a short wait.
normal.cn: just a moment 是请人稍等的客气说法。

normal.en: The adjective just is rare in speech but regular in law and argument.
normal.cn: 形容词 just 口语少用，但在法律和论证里很常见。

abstract.en: Just is a line laid exactly on a mark.
abstract.cn: just 就是把线正压在刻度上。

abstract.en: The same word measures time and measures fairness.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量时间，也量公平。

abstract.en: Exactness and justice are both a matter of not tipping the scale.
abstract.cn: 精确与公正，都是不让秤歪。

examples.en: The phone rang just as I sat down.
examples.cn: 我刚坐下电话就响了。

examples.en: He has just finished the last page.
examples.cn: 他刚刚看完最后一页。

examples.en: It was just a joke, nothing more.
examples.cn: 那只是个玩笑，没别的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎死特」—— 分寸掐得正正好，分毫不差

root: 拉丁语 jus「法、权利」→ justus「合法的、正当的」→ 古法语 juste → 英语 just；同族 justice、justify、justly。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: exactness in time, the immediate past, mere amount, fairness, bare sufficiency, and a softening request.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：时间或位置的恰好、刚刚过去、仅仅、公正、勉强够，以及缓和语气的「稍」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line set exactly on the mark, no slip either way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线正压在刻度上，两边都不偏。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: the train meets the moment you arrive.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：火车正好在你到时进站。

branches.en: THE PHONE: a call from a minute ago.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：一分钟前打来的。

branches.en: THE SMALL WORD: merely, and a gentle please wait.
branches.cn: 小小的语气词：仅仅，以及客气地请人稍等。

branches.en: THE SCALES: what someone deserves, to a hair.
branches.cn: 天平这条线：一个人应得的分毫不差。

branches.en: THE CLOSING GATE: through by a centimetre.
branches.cn: 关门这条线：差一厘米就进不来。

intro.en: Just is the bare Latin adjective; its family takes Latin and English endings.
intro.cn: just 是裸露的拉丁形容词，它的词族要加拉丁或英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jus, law, and justus, lawful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jus「法」与 justus「合法的」。

definition_zh: 正义；公正；公平；司法；审判；法官（头衔）
definition_en: the quality of being fair and right, or the system that courts use to decide what is right
core_image: 蒙眼的女像一手持天平，一手持剑，稳稳立在台阶之上
scene: 法院门口的台阶上，两排石柱之间刻着一句关于公平的铭文。The family is still waiting for justice after ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 justice 是「公正、正义」（第 1 个义项：公平正当的品质），句意为十年过去，这家人仍在等待公正。画面里的物件：法院、台阶、石刻铭文。

pos.zh: 名词：正义；公正；司法；审判；（法官头衔）大法官

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「公正的」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
同源动词，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 in- 构成，义为「不公正」
由 justice 派生，指司法官或司法机构

senses.title: Fairness as a quality
senses.definition: the quality of being fair and giving each person what is due
senses.definitionCN: 公平待人、各得其所的品质
senses.example: She fought for justice for the workers.
senses.exampleCN: 她为工人们争取公正。
senses.why: The core is fairness treated as a thing worth having and defending.
senses.whyCN: 核心是被当作值得争取与守护之物的公平。

senses.title: The system of courts
senses.definition: the legal system and the process of judging cases
senses.definitionCN: 法律体系以及审理案件的程序
senses.example: The case will go through the criminal justice system.
senses.exampleCN: 此案将走刑事司法程序。
senses.why: Fairness put into institutions becomes a system of courts and procedure.
senses.whyCN: 公平被装进机构，就变成法院与程序构成的体系。

senses.title: A fair outcome for someone
senses.definition: the fair result that a person has been denied or is owed
senses.definitionCN: 被剥夺或应得的那份公平结果
senses.example: The families finally got justice in court.
senses.exampleCN: 这些家庭终于在法庭上得到了公正。
senses.why: Here the abstract quality turns into a concrete settlement someone receives.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象的品质变成某人实际得到的结果。

senses.title: A title for a judge
senses.definition: a formal title for a judge of a high court
senses.definitionCN: 高等法院法官的正式头衔
senses.example: Justice Hill wrote the opinion for the court.
senses.exampleCN: 希尔大法官为法庭撰写了意见。
senses.why: A person who embodies fairness in court takes the abstract noun as a title.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上代表公平的人，直接拿了那个抽象名词当头衔。

senses.title: Fair treatment in presentation
senses.definition: the quality of doing full justice to a subject or a person
senses.definitionCN: 指充分、恰当呈现某题材或某人的水准
senses.example: The film does justice to a difficult story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影充分展现了那个难讲的故事。
senses.why: Giving a subject its due is the same fairness applied to description.
senses.whyCN: 把题材应得的分量给它，是公平用在了描写上。

senses.title: Rightness in judgement
senses.definition: the correctness of a decision or evaluation
senses.definitionCN: 指决定或评价的正确恰当
senses.example: There is some justice in his complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他的抱怨有几分道理。
senses.why: A verdict that measures correctly is justice in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 量得准确的一次判断，就是缩小的正义。

intro.en: Justice comes from Latin justitia, fairness, from justus, lawful, and jus, law, through Old French.
intro.cn: justice 来自拉丁语 justitia「公平」，源自 justus「合法的」与 jus「法」，经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: justitia named the quality of being just, and justus came from jus, law.
items.cn: justitia 指「公正的品质」，justus 源自 jus「法」。

items.en: Old French justise carried both fairness and the right to judge.
items.cn: 古法语 justise 同时带着公平与审判权两层意思。

items.en: English took justice in the twelfth century for fairness and the courts.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪借入 justice，指公平与法庭。

items.en: The title Justice for a high court judge settled in later use.
items.cn: 作为高院法官头衔的 Justice 在后世固定下来。

items.en: The phrase do justice to extended it to art and description.
items.cn: do justice to 这一说法把它延伸到艺术与描写。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin law root; the near-meaning group holds other words for fairness and law.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根；近义组收其他表示公平与法律的词。

entries.definition: Fair, or exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，义为「公正的」或「正好」。

entries.definition: To give good reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: Unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 加 in- 构成，义为「不公正」。

entries.definition: The quality of treating people equally.
entries.definitionCN: 最日常的「公平」，语气朴素。

entries.definition: Fairness, especially where equal treatment must be adjusted.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指衡平与实质公平。

entries.definition: The set of rules a society enforces.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会强制执行的法律规则本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from Latin jus to the steps of a courthouse.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语 jus「法」走到法院门前的台阶。

normal.en: The root jus, law, also gives just and justify.
normal.cn: 词根 jus「法」还生出 just 与 justify。

normal.en: Bring someone to justice means get them into court.
normal.cn: bring someone to justice 指把人送上法庭。

normal.en: Do justice to is about showing something fully.
normal.cn: do justice to 指把某物充分表现出来。

normal.en: Justice can mean both the quality and the courts.
normal.cn: justice 既指公正的品质，也指司法机关。

normal.en: Injustice is simply justice with in-.
normal.cn: injustice 就是 justice 加 in-。

abstract.en: Justice is a scale held steady by an unseen hand.
abstract.cn: 正义是一杆被看不见的手扶稳的秤。

abstract.en: The same word is a principle and a building.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既是原则也是一座建筑。

abstract.en: It is fairness given an address and a date.
abstract.cn: 它就是有了地址和日期的公平。

examples.en: They demanded justice for the victims.
examples.cn: 他们为受害者要求公正。

examples.en: The justice system is slow but open.
examples.cn: 司法体系运转缓慢但公开。

examples.en: No photograph can do justice to that valley.
examples.cn: 任何照片都无法展现那条山谷的全部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎斯蒂斯」—— 秤杆扎稳了，才有正义

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」→ justus「合法的」→ justitia「公正」→ 古法语 justise → 英语 justice；同族 just、justify、injustice。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: fairness as a quality, the court system, a fair outcome, a judge's title, full presentation, and the rightness of a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：公正的品质、司法体系、应得的公正结果、大法官头衔、充分展现，以及评判得当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blindfolded figure holding scales and a sword.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒙眼持秤与剑的女像。

branches.en: THE BANNER: a principle that people march for.
branches.cn: 旗帜这条线：人们为之游行的一条原则。

branches.en: THE COURTHOUSE: procedure, lawyers, and hours of waiting.
branches.cn: 法院这条线：程序、律师和漫长的等待。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: a fair result handed to a family.
branches.cn: 裁决这条线：交到家属手里的公正结果。

branches.en: THE BENCH: a title spoken with a name.
branches.cn: 法官席这条线：念出姓氏的头衔。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: a work that shows its subject fully and fairly.
branches.cn: 作品这条线：完整而恰当地表现题材。

intro.en: Justice adds a Latin-derived noun ending to just; the deeper pieces are jus and justus.
intro.cn: justice 给 just 加了一个拉丁来源的名词词尾，更深的部件是 jus 与 justus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jus, law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jus「法」。

items.example: A just ruler weighs both sides.
items.exampleCN: 公正的统治者会称量两边。

definition_zh: 证明……正当；为……辩护；使合理化；调整使排满（排版）
definition_en: to show that something is right or reasonable, or to give a good reason for it
core_image: 有人举起一张纸，一条一条向对面的人解释为什么这样做没错
scene: 会议室里被质问的一方把证据摊开，逐条说明当初的决定为什么合理。Nothing can justify that much expense on one dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 justify 是「证明……正当」（第 1 个义项：给出理由说明某事合理），句意为没有任何理由能为一顿晚饭花那么多钱开脱。画面里的物件：会议室、证据文件、对面的听众。

pos.zh: 动词：证明正当；为……辩解；使合理；（排版）使两端对齐

derivatives.zh: 由 justify 加 -cation 构成，义为「辩护；正当理由」
由 justify 加 -ed 构成，义为「有正当理由的」
由 justify 加 -able 构成，义为「可辩解的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「无正当理由的」

senses.title: To show that something is right
senses.definition: to give reasons that show an action or claim is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由以证明某行为或主张合理
senses.example: How do you justify spending so much on a phone?
senses.exampleCN: 你凭什么为花这么多钱买手机找理由？
senses.why: The word sets a thing on the scale of right and asks whether it balances.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一件事放上「正当」的秤，问它是否配平。

senses.title: To defend against criticism
senses.definition: to answer criticism by defending a choice or statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过辩护某个选择或说法来回应批评
senses.example: The manager justified his decision to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 经理向全队为自己的决定作了辩解。
senses.why: Justifying is talking back to an accusation with reasons.
senses.whyCN: 辩解就是用理由回应一项指责。

senses.title: To be a good reason for
senses.definition: to be the reason that makes something acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 本身构成使某事可接受的理由
senses.example: The delay was justified by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误因暴风雨而有其理由。
senses.why: Here the subject is the reason itself, not the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里作主语的是理由本身，而不是说话的人。

senses.title: To set text flush at the margins
senses.definition: in printing, to space text so that both edges line up
senses.definitionCN: 排版中调整字距，使左右两边都对齐
senses.example: The columns are justified so the page looks tidy.
senses.exampleCN: 各栏都两端对齐，页面显得整齐。
senses.why: Typesetting sets lines to exact margins, the same exactness the word always carried.
senses.whyCN: 排版把行对齐到精确的边界，正是这个词一直带有的「精确」。

senses.title: To prove oneself right by result
senses.definition: to be shown right by later events
senses.definitionCN: 指后来的事实说明当初是对的
senses.example: The final score justified the coach's choice.
senses.exampleCN: 最终比分证明了教练的选择。
senses.why: Later facts can do the weighing that argument could not.
senses.whyCN: 后来发生的事实能做论证做不到的那次称量。

senses.title: To declare someone righteous
senses.definition: in theology, to declare a person righteous before God
senses.definitionCN: 神学中指宣告某人在神面前为义
senses.example: The doctrine says faith alone justifies the believer.
senses.exampleCN: 该教义说唯凭信使信徒称义。
senses.why: The theological sense is a declaration of rightness rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 神学义是一种宣告其为义，而不是去证明。

intro.en: Justify is Latin justus, right, plus facere, to make: to make right or to show as right.
intro.cn: justify 是拉丁语 justus「正当的」加 facere「做」：使之正当，或显示其为正当。

items.en: justificare meant to make just or to do justice, from justus and facere.
items.cn: justificare 意为使之公正或伸张正义，由 justus 与 facere 组成。

items.en: The -fic- element is a form of facere, to make or do.
items.cn: -fic- 部分是 facere「做」的形式，广见于 -ify 动词。

items.en: English borrowed justify in the fourteenth century for legal defence.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 justify，最初用于法律辩护。

items.en: The theological sense of being declared righteous developed in the Reformation.
items.cn: 「称义」的神学义在宗教改革时期发展起来。

items.en: The printing sense arrived with mechanical typesetting.
items.cn: 排版义随机械排字而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ify pattern and the justice root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of defending and explaining.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ify 构词与 justice 词根；近义组收辩护与解释类动词。

entries.definition: Fairness or the court system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: One who gives a defence.
entries.definitionCN: 由 justify 加 -er 构成，指辩解者。

entries.definition: A reason given in defence.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「正当理由」。

entries.definition: To protect or argue for something attacked.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵御或为受攻者辩护。

entries.definition: To make something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事情说清楚，不必涉及对错。

entries.definition: To try to lessen the blame for something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为减轻过错找借口。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from justus plus facere to justified text on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 justus 加 facere 走到页面上两端对齐的文字。

normal.en: Justify is just plus -ify, which comes from facere, to make.
normal.cn: justify 是 just 加 -ify，后者来自 facere「做」。

normal.en: The -ify ending also appears in testify and simplify.
normal.cn: -ify 词尾也见于 testify 与 simplify。

normal.en: Justify doing something is the common pattern.
normal.cn: justify doing something 是常见搭配。

normal.en: The noun is justification, not justifation.
normal.cn: 名词是 justification，不是 justifation。

normal.en: Justified text lines up on both sides.
normal.cn: justified text 指左右两边都对齐的文字。

abstract.en: To justify is to hand the scale a weight that balances.
abstract.cn: 辩护就是往秤另一头放上配得上的砝码。

abstract.en: A reason that fits exactly is justice at the level of argument.
abstract.cn: 恰好配平的理由，就是论证层面的正义。

abstract.en: Some things cannot be weighed at all.
abstract.cn: 有些事根本没法上秤。

examples.en: Nothing can justify hiding the report.
examples.cn: 没有任何理由能为隐瞒报告开脱。

examples.en: She was justified in refusing the offer.
examples.cn: 她拒绝这个提议是有道理的。

examples.en: Justify the whole paragraph to make it look clean.
examples.cn: 把整段两端对齐，看起来更整齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「just 我 fi」—— 站得正，才敢说「我没错」

root: 拉丁语 justus「正当的」+ facere「做」→ justificare「使之正当」→ 英语 justify；名词 justification。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: showing something right, defending it, being the reason for it, aligning text, being proved right, and being declared righteous.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：证明合理、为决定辩护、构成理由、文字两端对齐、以结果证明，以及宗教上的「称义」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reasons laid on a scale until it balances.
core.cn: 核心意象：把理由放到秤上，直到配平。

branches.en: THE SCALE: reasons heavy enough to hold the act up.
branches.cn: 秤这条线：理由够重，撑得住那个行为。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a decision explained to those who question it.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：向质疑者解释决定。

branches.en: THE PAGE: every line lands on both margins.
branches.cn: 页面这条线：每一行都落在两边边界上。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: the result that settles the argument.
branches.cn: 记分牌这条线：结果把争论定下。

branches.en: THE PULPIT: the doctrine of being made righteous.
branches.cn: 讲坛这条线：称义的教义。

intro.en: Justify is just plus the Latin verb ending -ify, from facere.
intro.cn: justify 是 just 加拉丁动词词尾 -ify，源自 facere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus through justus and from facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus（经 justus）与 facere。

definition_zh: 热切的；渴望的；敏锐的；锋利的；激烈的
definition_en: very eager to do something, or sharp in mind, sense, or edge
core_image: 刀口在光下反出一道细白线，一眼看去就让人缩手
scene: 雪后清早，几个人在门口换鞋，谁都想第一个上坡。The children are keen to see the snow before it melts.
sceneCN: 这里 keen 是「热切的、渴望的」（第 1 个义项：非常想做某事），句意为孩子们急着想在雪化前去看雪。画面里的物件：门口、雪、换鞋的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：热切的；渴望的；敏锐的；锋利的；激烈的

derivatives.zh: 由 keen 加 -ly 构成，义为「热切地；敏锐地」
由 keen 加 -ness 构成，义为「热心；锐利」

senses.title: Very eager to do something
senses.definition: very much wanting to do something or to have something happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常想做某事或希望某事发生
senses.example: He was keen to start work that same week.
senses.exampleCN: 他迫切想当周就开始工作。
senses.why: The sharp edge of wanting points forward at the thing not yet had.
senses.whyCN: 渴望那道「锋刃」朝前指着还没到手的那个东西。

senses.title: Sharp in mind or sense
senses.definition: quick to notice, understand, or feel
senses.definitionCN: 注意、理解或感受得很快
senses.example: She has a keen ear for small changes in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对语调里的细微变化很敏感。
senses.why: A faculty described as keen is one that cuts into detail.
senses.whyCN: 被称作 keen 的能力，是能切进细节的那种能力。

senses.title: Sharp in edge
senses.definition: having a fine, cutting edge
senses.definitionCN: 指刀刃又细又快
senses.example: The knife is keen enough to cut paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀快得能切纸。
senses.why: This is the literal edge from which all the other senses borrow their sharpness.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的刃口，其他各义的「锐利」都从这里借来。

senses.title: Intense or strong in feeling
senses.definition: strong and intense, as of competition, interest, or wind
senses.definitionCN: 指竞争、兴趣或风等强烈而凌厉
senses.example: Competition for the place was keen.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名额的竞争很激烈。
senses.why: Intensity is pressure concentrated on a narrow point, like an edge.
senses.whyCN: 强度就是集中在一点上的压力，像一条刃。

senses.title: Bitter and cold, of weather
senses.definition: piercingly cold, as of wind
senses.definitionCN: 指风等冷得刺人
senses.example: A keen wind came off the water.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上吹来一阵刺骨的风。
senses.why: A wind that feels sharp is weather described with the edge image.
senses.whyCN: 感觉锋利的风，是用刃的画面去写天气。

senses.title: A wailing lament for the dead
senses.definition: a loud lament for a dead person, chiefly Irish usage
senses.definitionCN: 主要指爱尔兰习俗中为死者发出的哭号
senses.example: The women raised a keen over the body.
senses.exampleCN: 妇女们为遗体唱起挽歌。
senses.why: This noun is a separate borrowing, though the cry is high and piercing like the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是另一次借词，但那种哭声高而尖，与形容词的感觉相通。

intro.en: Keen comes from Old English cene, meaning bold and brave, and only later took on sharpness and eagerness.
intro.cn: keen 来自古英语 cene「勇敢的」，较晚才发展出「锋利、热切」等义。

items.en: cene meant bold, brave, or fierce in battle.
items.cn: cene 意为战斗中勇敢、勇猛。

items.en: Middle English kene widened to sharp, severe, and quick.
items.cn: 中古英语 kene 扩展到尖锐、严厉、敏捷。

items.en: Related Norse forms reinforced the sense of sharpness and edge.
items.cn: 相关的古北欧语形式加强了「锐利」的感觉。

items.en: The eagerness sense settled in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「热切」义在十九世纪固定下来。

items.en: The noun keen for a lament came from Irish caoineadh.
items.cn: 表示挽歌的名词 keen 来自爱尔兰语 caoineadh。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that look like keen; the near-meaning group holds adjectival first cousins.
note.cn: 形近组收外形容易与 keen 混的短词；近义组收几个形容词近亲。

entries.definition: To have or hold something.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「保持；保留」，来源不同。

entries.definition: A small barrel.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，指小桶。

entries.definition: A small twist or tight bend.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「扭结；小弯」，来源不同。

entries.definition: Wanting something very much.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「渴望的」，与第 1 个义项最近。

entries.definition: Having a fine edge or quick mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「锋利的；机敏的」。

entries.definition: Very sharp or very strong.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指极为敏锐或强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a brave fighter to a knife and then to a keen student.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从勇敢的战士走到刀刃，再走到热心的学生。

normal.en: Old English cene meant brave, not eager.
normal.cn: 古英语 cene 意为勇敢，而不是热切。

normal.en: Keen on is the preposition for interest, as in keen on music.
normal.cn: 表示兴趣用 keen on，如 keen on music。

normal.en: Keen to do takes the infinitive.
normal.cn: keen to do 后接动词不定式。

normal.en: A keen eye is a sharp eye, not an eager one.
normal.cn: a keen eye 指眼力锐利，不是心急。

normal.en: The Irish keen is a wail over the dead.
normal.cn: 爱尔兰语来源的 keen 是为逝者哭号。

abstract.en: Keen is a blade of attention.
abstract.cn: keen 是注意力磨出的刃口。

abstract.en: Sharp edge, sharp mind, sharp wind: one image, three places.
abstract.cn: 刃利、头脑利、风利：一个比喻用在三处。

abstract.en: The eager and the edged share their keenness.
abstract.cn: 渴望与锋锐共用同一份「利」。

examples.en: She is keen on learning another language.
examples.cn: 她很热衷于学另一门语言。

examples.en: The blade was still keen after years of use.
examples.cn: 这把刀用了多年依然锋利。

examples.en: They have a keen sense of what is fair.
examples.cn: 他们对什么算公平有很敏锐的直觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」—— 肯去做的人，才是热切的

root: 古英语 cene「勇敢的、勇猛的」→ 中古英语 kene「尖锐的、敏捷的」→ 现代英语 keen「锋利；敏锐；热切」；挽歌义另来自爱尔兰语 caoineadh。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: eager, sharp-minded, sharp-edged, intense, bitingly cold, and the Irish lament.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：热切、敏锐、锋利、强烈、刺骨的冷，以及爱尔兰的挽歌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine bright edge that makes you draw your hand back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道细亮的刃口，让人本能地缩手。

branches.en: THE STAIRS: children pushing to be first up.
branches.cn: 楼梯这条线：孩子们抢着先上去。

branches.en: THE EAR: catching a change no one else noticed.
branches.cn: 耳朵这条线：听出别人漏掉的细微变化。

branches.en: THE EDGE AND THE WIND: both cut a little.
branches.cn: 刀刃与风这条线：两者都能割一下。

branches.en: THE MARKET: competition that presses hard.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：紧逼的竞争。

branches.en: THE WAKE: a cry that rises over a body.
branches.cn: 守灵这条线：在遗体上响起的哭声。

intro.en: Keen is a native English adjective and takes only English endings.
intro.cn: keen 是英语本族形容词，只加英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Keen has no Latin root, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: keen 没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 保持；保存；保留；继续；饲养；遵守；照料
definition_en: to continue to have or hold something, or to stay in a state without changing
core_image: 手里紧紧攥着一样东西，怎么也不松
scene: 搬家时他把一箱旧信留在角落，谁劝也不肯扔。He kept every letter she ever sent him.
sceneCN: 这里 keep 是「保存、保留」（第 2 个义项：留着不丢弃），句意为她寄来的每封信他都留着。画面里的物件：一箱旧信、搬家纸箱、角落。

pos.zh: 动词：保持；保留；保存；继续；饲养；遵守
名词：生计；饲养费用（keep of a horse）

derivatives.zh: 由 keep 加 -er 构成，义为「看守人；守门员」
由 keep 加 -ing 构成，义为「保管；一致」
由 up 加 keep 构成，义为「维护费用」
复合名词，义为「妥善保管」

senses.title: To stay in a state
senses.definition: to continue to be in a particular state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 继续处在某种状态
senses.example: Keep calm and read the question again.
senses.exampleCN: 保持冷静，把题目再读一遍。
senses.why: The core is continuation: the state does not change.
senses.whyCN: 核心是延续：状态不发生变化。

senses.title: To retain possession of
senses.definition: to continue to have something and not give it away or lose it
senses.definitionCN: 继续拥有某物，不送出也不丢失
senses.example: You can keep the book; I have another copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书你留着吧，我还有一本。
senses.why: Retaining is continuation applied to an object in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 保留就是把「延续」用在手里的一件东西上。

senses.title: To do something repeatedly
senses.definition: to continue doing something, often again and again
senses.definitionCN: 持续做某事，常指一再发生
senses.example: She kept looking at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直朝门口看。
senses.why: Repeating an act is continuing it, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 反复做同一个动作就是把它延续下去，同一个动词因此兼顾两者。

senses.title: To care for or raise animals
senses.definition: to own and look after animals such as bees or chickens
senses.definitionCN: 指拥有并照料蜜蜂、鸡等动物
senses.example: They keep bees behind the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在谷仓后面养蜂。
senses.why: Looking after animals is holding them over time, at a steady cost.
senses.whyCN: 照料动物就是长期持有，并付出持续的开销。

senses.title: To observe or honour a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, promise, or custom
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、承诺或习俗去做
senses.example: Everyone kept the silence until the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 大家一直保持安静，直到铃响。
senses.why: Honouring a rule is keeping it in force, the same holding seen from the rule side.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是让规则继续有效，是同一个「持有」从规则那边看。

senses.title: The cost of living or upkeep
senses.definition: the food and cost needed to maintain a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 维持人或动物所需的食物与花费
senses.example: The keep of a horse is no small sum.
senses.exampleCN: 养一匹马的开销可不小。
senses.why: The noun names what must be handed over to keep something alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指为了把某物养活下去必须付出的东西。

intro.en: Keep comes from Old English cepan, to seize or take heed, and the sense shifted from grabbing to holding.
intro.cn: keep 来自古英语 cepan「抓住、留意」，词义从「抓取」滑向「持有」。

items.en: cepan meant to seize, to take heed, or to watch over.
items.cn: cepan 意为抓取、留意或看守。

items.en: The sense of watching gave keepers and keeping guard.
items.cn: 「看守」义后来生出 keeper 与 keep guard。

items.en: Middle English keep broadened to hold, retain, and continue.
items.cn: 中古英语 keep 扩展到持有、保留、持续。

items.en: Keep doing became the standard pattern for continuing an action.
items.cn: keep doing 成为表示「持续做」的标准结构。

items.en: The noun keep survives in the keep of an animal and in upkeep.
items.cn: 名词 keep 保留在动物饲养费与 upkeep 中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short look-alikes of keep; the near-meaning group holds verbs of holding and continuing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 keep 相似的短词；近义组收表示持有与持续的词。

entries.definition: Eager or sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「热切的；锋利的」。

entries.definition: The past form of keep.
entries.definitionCN: keep 的过去式和过去分词。

entries.definition: Someone who looks after something.
entries.definitionCN: 由 keep 加 -er 构成，指看守人或守门员。

entries.definition: To have something in the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 指手里拿着，最具体。

entries.definition: To keep something in good condition.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指维持良好状态。

entries.definition: To keep something rather than lose it.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，强调不失去。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from Old English cepan, to seize, to a box of letters in the corner.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从古英语 cepan「抓取」走到角落那箱旧信。

normal.en: Old English cepan meant to seize and also to watch over.
normal.cn: 古英语 cepan 既指抓取，也指看守。

normal.en: Keep doing means keep on doing, without a break.
normal.cn: keep doing 意为一再做，不间断。

normal.en: Kept is the only past form; there is no keeped.
normal.cn: 过去式只有 kept，没有 keeped。

normal.en: Keeper adds -er to make the person.
normal.cn: keeper 加 -er 变成人。

normal.en: Keep in touch fixes the retaining sense in daily use.
normal.cn: keep in touch 把「保持」义留在日常里。

abstract.en: To keep is to refuse to let the moment pass.
abstract.cn: 保留就是不让那一刻过去。

abstract.en: The same word holds an object, a habit, and a silence.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能留住东西、习惯和一份安静。

abstract.en: A keeper is one who holds a door open for others.
abstract.cn: keeper 是替别人扶住门的人。

examples.en: Please keep the door closed at night.
examples.cn: 夜里请把门关着。

examples.en: She kept the old ticket in her wallet.
examples.cn: 她一直把那张旧票留在钱包里。

examples.en: He kept asking the same question.
examples.cn: 他一直在问同一个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「k皮」—— 把皮牢牢攥住，就是保留下来

root: 古英语 cepan「抓取；留意；看守」→ 中古英语 keep「持有；保留；继续」→ 现代英语 keep；过去式 kept。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: staying in a state, retaining an object, doing something repeatedly, keeping animals, obeying a rule, and the cost of upkeep.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：保持状态、保留物件、一再做某事、饲养动物、遵守规则，以及饲养费用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closed tight around something, not letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：手紧紧攥住一样东西，不放手。

branches.en: THE SHUT DOOR: a state left exactly as it was.
branches.cn: 关着的门这条线：状态原封不动。

branches.en: THE BOX OF LETTERS: things kept and never thrown out.
branches.cn: 信箱这条线：留着从不丢的东西。

branches.en: THE REPEATED QUESTION: an action that goes on.
branches.cn: 反复的提问这条线：持续不断的行为。

branches.en: THE HIVES: animals looked after, at a cost.
branches.cn: 蜂箱这条线：照料动物，也要花钱。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: a rule held to without exception.
branches.cn: 承诺这条线：不打折扣地遵守。

intro.en: Keep is a native verb; English endings build its family with no Latin stem.
intro.cn: keep 是本族动词，词族全靠英语词尾，没有拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind keep, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: keep 背后没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 水壶；（烧水用的）壶；一壶的量
definition_en: a metal or plastic container with a handle and a spout, used for boiling water
core_image: 炉架上一只带弯嘴的金属壶，壶嘴正冒着白汽
scene: 清晨厨房里，炉子上的壶刚开始鸣响，窗户蒙上一层雾。Put the kettle on; we will have tea before we go.
sceneCN: 这里 kettle 是「水壶」（第 1 个义项：烧水用的带柄带嘴容器），句意为把水壶坐上，我们出门前喝杯茶。画面里的物件：厨房、炉子、起雾的窗。

pos.zh: 名词：水壶；一壶的量

derivatives.zh: 由 kettle 加 -ful 构成，义为「一壶之量」
复合词，指定音鼓，形如倒扣的壶

senses.title: A vessel for boiling water
senses.definition: a container with a lid, handle, and spout, used to boil water
senses.definitionCN: 有盖、柄和壶嘴，用来烧水的容器
senses.example: The kettle began to whistle on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 炉子上的水壶开始呜呜叫。
senses.why: The core object is a vessel built for one job: turning water into steam.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一只专做一件事的容器：把水变成蒸汽。

senses.title: The amount it holds
senses.definition: as much water as such a vessel can hold
senses.definitionCN: 这样一只壶能装下的水量
senses.example: We drank a whole kettle of tea before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午之前我们喝了整整一壶茶。
senses.why: A container easily becomes a unit of measure for what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 容器很容易变成衡量所装之物的单位。

senses.title: A large metal pot for boiling
senses.definition: a large open metal vessel for boiling food or washing, as in older households
senses.definitionCN: 旧时家庭用来煮食物或洗衣的大金属容器
senses.example: The laundry went into the copper kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 要洗的衣服被扔进紫铜大锅。
senses.why: The old large-pot sense survives where the work was done in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 「大锅」这个旧义保留在工作成批进行的地方。

senses.title: A kettle-shaped drum
senses.definition: a drum made of a metal bowl, in the compound kettledrum
senses.definitionCN: 由金属碗状鼓身做成，见复合词 kettledrum
senses.example: The kettledrums opened the march.
senses.exampleCN: 定音鼓为进行曲开场。
senses.why: A drum made of a metal bowl looks exactly like an upturned kettle.
senses.whyCN: 用金属碗做鼓身的鼓，看上去就是倒扣的壶。

senses.title: A group of hawks in flight
senses.definition: a flock of birds of prey circling together on the wind
senses.definitionCN: 指盘旋在气流上的一群猛禽
senses.example: A kettle of hawks rose above the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一群鹰在山脊上空盘旋升起。
senses.why: Birds circling in a rising column suggest something stirring in a pot.
senses.whyCN: 飞鸟在上升气流里盘旋，像锅中翻动的东西。

intro.en: Kettle comes from Old Norse ketill and Latin catillus, a small dish, a word that travelled with the metal itself.
intro.cn: kettle 来自古北欧语 ketill 与拉丁语 catillus「小碟」，这个词是随金属器具一起传播的。

items.en: catillus was a small dish or bowl, from catinus, a deep vessel.
items.cn: catillus 意为小碟或小碗，来自 catinus「深容器」。

items.en: Old Norse ketill named a cauldron, borrowed from Latin-speaking traders.
items.cn: 古北欧语 ketill 指大锅，是从说拉丁语的商人那里借来的。

items.en: Old English cetel and cytel named a cooking pot.
items.cn: 古英语 cetel、cytel 指炊事用锅。

items.en: The form kettle fixed by the Middle English period.
items.cn: kettle 的拼写在中古英语时期固定下来。

items.en: The tea kettle sense dominated once tea became common.
items.cn: 茶普及之后，「烧水壶」义占据主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds vessels and short words close in shape; the near-meaning group holds other water vessels.
note.cn: 形近组收器物与外形相近的词；近义组收其他盛水器具。

entries.definition: Cows and bulls kept on a farm.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一字母，义为「牛群」。

entries.definition: As much as a kettle holds.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kettle 加 -ful 构成，指一壶之量。

entries.definition: Young cats.
entries.definitionCN: 发音相近，义为「小猫」。

entries.definition: A deep round container for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 指较深的锅或罐。

entries.definition: A pot in which tea is made.
entries.definitionCN: 指沏茶的茶壶，通常不上炉。

entries.definition: A large open pot over a fire.
entries.definitionCN: 多用于文学，指火上的大锅。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a Latin small dish to the whistle before tea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「小碟」走到沏茶前的一声鸣响。

normal.en: The same word family gave cauldron through French.
normal.cn: 同一词族经由法语还生出 cauldron。

normal.en: Put the kettle on is a whole offer of tea in four words.
